exposure: HBsAg positive vs. negative women in all age groups
Women with pre-pregnancy BMI underweight and obesity aged <25 years and ≥35 years vs. other age groups
outcome: Prevalence of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP)
cohort: 39,742 pregnant women from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2019
finding: Several factors were associated with an increased risk of ICP, including maternal age <25 years and ≥35 years, pre-pregnancy underweight and obesity, HBsAg positive status, twin pregnancies, low maternal education, inadequate gestational weight gain, multiparous, in vitro fertilization, caesarean section history and the number of abortions ≥2, and ICP was associated with increased risk of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The presence of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) was associated with an increased risk of cesarean section and preterm birth.
